stories.delivered_paragraph: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said the company has never sought a blanket ban on open-weight AI models, pushing back against criticism that its closed-model business wants to restrict competitors. The dispute has gained urgency as Chinese open-weight systems approach frontier performance and U.S. officials consider possible restrictions.

stories.delivered_paragraph: New Line Cinema won a bidding war involving at least 10 parties for “Jealous People Are Ugly People,” a horror project from Greek-British filmmaker Theo James Krekis. Krekis will adapt and direct the feature from his BBC-commissioned short, which follows a man whose envy of a friend’s career success feeds a supernatural force. The sale reflects Hollywood’s intensified hunt for digital-first horror creators after recent low-budget genre breakouts set box-office records for their studios.

stories.delivered_paragraph: X has begun rolling out X Money in the United States to Premium and Premium Plus subscribers, expanding Elon Musk’s effort to turn the social platform into an “everything app.” The service offers a digital wallet, peer-to-peer payments, a metal Visa card and free transfers, while advertising yields of up to 6% APY for eligible users. Its move beyond an invite-only beta puts consumer-finance and security safeguards under greater scrutiny, including from lawmakers who have raised concerns.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warned that companies relying entirely on proprietary AI providers risk surrendering the data and institutional knowledge needed to remain competitive. Speaking on CNN, he said businesses should retain metadata from their model use so it can help train their own models or open-weight systems, rather than “outsourc[ing] your thinking.” The comments frame AI control and data ownership as strategic issues for customers even as they adopt tools from major model makers.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Seattle police now believe at least three people fired shots during Sunday’s shooting at the Bite of Seattle festival near the Space Needle, revising their initial account of two shooters. Three people were killed and at least four wounded, including a two-year-old; one suspected shooter, 15, was arrested, another is believed dead at the scene, and police are seeking at least one more. The expanded investigation leaves key questions about the gunfight and its participants unresolved.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Small businesses have filed new lawsuits challenging the Trump administration’s latest import tariffs, which impose rates of 10% or 12.5% on goods from more than 60 economies. The plaintiffs include spice seller Burlap & Barrel, watch retailer Collective Horology and toymaker Learning Resources, which previously won a Supreme Court case over tariffs imposed under a different authority. The suits test the administration’s use of Section 301 after temporary Section 122 levies expired last week.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A federal magistrate judge has ordered Donald Trump’s trust to provide the BBC with some business financial records in the network’s defense against the president’s $10 billion defamation lawsuit. Judge Enjoliqué Aytch Lett granted the BBC’s request to compel documents only in part, limiting the subpoena’s scope. The ruling gives the BBC access to evidence relevant to damages while preventing the broader financial discovery it had sought.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Chinese officials responding to Typhoon Noul and recent floods are also confronting AI-generated videos that falsely show bodies in floodwaters, severe inundation and emergency measures. In some areas, bogus reports of power outages prompted panic buying, while fake images of crocodiles circulated after real flooding released hundreds of snakes from a breeding farm in Guangxi. The misinformation can complicate evacuations and rescue work by amplifying fear during already dangerous disasters.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Senior U.S. officials believe the Trump administration’s economic pressure campaign may inflict more lasting damage on Iran than its 13-day bombing campaign, citing signs of a worsening internal crisis including gasoline shortages. Trump paused strikes over the weekend and said Tehran had sought talks, a claim Iran denied, while Oman, Qatar and Pakistan mediate. Negotiators are trying to turn the pause into a durable ceasefire amid discussions that include traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A Los Angeles judge ruled that singer D4vd, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, will stand trial on murder charges in the death of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Prosecutors allege Burke stabbed and dismembered the girl after years of sexual abuse; her remains were found last September in a Tesla registered to his address. Burke, 21, has pleaded not guilty, with arraignment set for August 31 and trial expected within 90 days afterward.

stories.delivered_paragraph: “Obsession” star Michael Johnston is in early talks to join Universal’s fourth “Mummy” film alongside returning leads Brendan Fraser and Rachel Weisz. stories.delivered_paragraph: Investors are scrutinizing a report that Nvidia could backstop an OpenAI data-center lease, an arrangement that would reportedly be the largest of its kind. One analyst warned that such a deal could revive a troubling tech-bubble practice, likely because it would deepen financial ties between a dominant chip supplier and a major customer. The concern matters as markets assess whether AI infrastructure demand is independently sustainable or being reinforced by circular financing.
